task_summary: Continue the fan ESC assessment: distinguish power wiring from control wiring using manufacturer drawings and owner clarification.

acceptance: Resolve whether the owner connected power or a control signal there.
Avoid hardware changes before the actual ESC control connection is identified.
completed: Manufacturer schematic pages 4 and 5 and the original silkscreen agree: power output and ESC control header are separate.
Owner clarified that DCOUT carries the two power leads; no incorrect signal connection is established.
One native worker and the coordinator visually checked the source drawings.
remaining: Identify the actual ESC control connection and match its board documentation before firmware implementation.

metrics.name: followup_observed_interval
metrics.basis: First follow-up clock through cutoff; excludes prior assessment round time.

metrics.name: native_workers
metrics.basis: Read-only drawing review; no extra Opus call.

observations: This is supplementary evidence to the same fan assessment, not a separate implementation or hardware test.
Owner terminology initially conflated power with signal; a bounded clarification resolved that ambiguity without alleging damage.
One primary website address failed; its official alternate served the same manufacturer README.
Worker text extraction failed; direct PDF rendering and visual inspection established the pin functions.

recommendations.action: Identify a wire by its endpoint label and electrical function before diagnosing an incorrect connection; do not infer pinout from color or chip family.
recommendations.next_check: Compare actual ESC and control-header labels before adapting the output.

limits: Exact installed ESC board and signal connector remain unverified.
Generic reference-board timing is not confirmation of this device compatibility.
No firmware edits, flashing, live measurements or motor operation.
No matched quality baseline; no speedup claim.
